items.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: Basie was going on a very important tour in Sweden for over a month. And Sonny Payne got very ill.

ctx.x: Well what was your first association with Count Basie?

The first time with Basie? Let me see. It was actually when I joined Norman Granz, Jazz at the Philharmonic. I had known Basie before that because in 1951 he’d been appearing in New York at the Strand Theater and we were at Birdland, right across the street. And he used to come down and his own words were “I went straight to the bar and put my head down and with my hands around my head, and just listened to you guys, and getting madder and madder as I heard all of this great music coming out of that band.” You…

we’ll fix it out Lou, I’ll take care of your guys and you can play the gig when you get back.” So I did about five weeks with that band and recorded with them. And that was like Ellington’s band, just a tremendous experience. I was talking to Frank Wess about that today because he was on the band, and also Benny Powell. And Basie during that time was trying to straighten himself out, not too much alcohol. And he knew that I didn’t drink and I had some goodies in my bag at all times to munch on. Because over there…

items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Sonny Payne was great. I know he was a master showman, throwing the sticks up in the air, but that was a gimmick. But he could really play.

ctx.x: When I first heard him play – that four-bar break he made on – with Basie’s Band – Queer Street, that’s a classic. Today there’s a guy around called Harold Jones that’s another fabulous drummer. He lives up here. He can really play. He’ll swing you into bad health too. He knows that book. Sonny Payne was great. I know he was a master showman, throwing the sticks up in the air, but that was a gimmick. But he could really play. That Atomic album that Neal Hefti wrote for Basie, Sonny really played well on that.
Let’s go back and talk about that sextet that you co-led with Charlie Shavers. Who else was in that band?
